facts.statement: Alcmonavis lived in the area of present-day Germany during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: during the Late Jurassic lived in the area of present Germany

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered by amateur paleontologist Roland Pöschl at the Alte Schöpfel quarry near Mörnsheim in Bavaria.
facts.quote: Amateur paleontologist Roland Pöschl systematically excavated the Alte Schöpfel quarry on the Schaudiberg, at Mühlheim near Mörnsheim in Bavaria

facts.statement: The fossil slab showing a right wing was discovered in November 2017.
facts.quote: In November 2017, he discovered a slab showing a right wing of a primordial bird

facts.statement: The species Alcmonavis poeschli was named and described in 2019 by Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut, Helmut Tischlinger, and Christian Foth.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species Alcmonavis poeschli was named and described by Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut, Helmut Tischlinger and Christian Foth

facts.statement: The holotype fossil consists of a nearly complete but partially articulated right wing.
facts.quote: It consists of a nearly complete but only partially articulated right wing

facts.statement: The holotype was estimated to be 111% the length of the largest known Archaeopteryx specimen.
facts.quote: The length of the holotype was estimated at 111% of that of the largest known Archaeopteryx specimen, the Solnhofener exemplar

facts.statement: The estimated length of the humerus is about nine centimeters.
facts.quote: The estimated humerus length is about nine centimetres

facts.statement: The humerus features a large deltopectoral crest whose expansion exceeds the shaft width.
facts.quote: The humerus has a large deltopectoral crest, the expansion of which exceeds the shaft width

facts.statement: The ulna possesses a single, clearly distinct oval depression on its upper articulation surface.
facts.quote: The ulna has a single and clearly distinct oval depression in its upper articulation surface

facts.statement: Some researchers still argue that the original fossil was a specimen of Archaeopteryx rather than a new species.
facts.quote: a classification still argued by some researchers

facts.statement: In early 2026, O'Connor and Marugán-Lobón argued that Alcmonavis and Ostromia are junior synonyms of Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: In early 2026, O'Connor and Marugán-Lobón regarded Alcmonavis and Ostromia as junior synonyms of Archaeopteryx

facts.statement: Alcmonavis lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 145.06 million years ago)
